package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"runtime"
	"sort"

	"github.com/prince776/go-dst-kit/realworld"
)

var __w = realworld.New(realworld.Options{})

type val struct{ x int }

func (v val) show(out chan<- string)   { out <- fmt.Sprint("value receiver: ", v.x) }
func (v *val) showP(out chan<- string) { out <- fmt.Sprint("pointer receiver: ", v.x) }

type holder struct{ fn func(chan<- string) }

func say(s string) func(chan<- string) { return func(out chan<- string) { out <- s } }

func show(what string, n int, out chan<- string) { out <- fmt.Sprint(what, ": ", n) }

// Each go statement's operands change right after it; the goroutines run
// only once main blocks (one P), so they see the new values unless their
// operands were evaluated at the go statement, as Go does.
func main() {
	runtime.GOMAXPROCS(1)
	out := make(chan string, 16)

	n := 1
	go show("variable", n, out)
	n++

	v := val{x: 1}
	go v.show(out)
	v.x = 2

	p := &val{x: 1}
	go p.show(out) // value method through a pointer: *p is copied now
	p.x = 2

	q := &val{x: 1}
	other := &val{x: 2}
	go q.showP(out)
	q = other
	_ = q

	f := say("func variable: 1")
	go f(out)
	f = say("func variable: 2")
	_ = f

	h := holder{fn: say("func field: 1")}
	go h.fn(out)
	h.fn = say("func field: 2")

	k := 1 // never changed: needs no binding
	go show("stable", k, out)

	r := &val{x: 1} // changed only through the pointer: r needs no binding
	go r.showP(out)
	r.x = 1

	var got []string
	for range 8 {
		got = append(got, <-out)
	}
	sort.Strings(got)
	for _, s := range got {
		fmt.Println(s)
	}
}
